doc.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Pontiac's size and joining the Boy Scouts
summary: He gives the town's population and describes a World War I veteran scoutmaster who taught discipline.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: About what do you think the population of Pontiac was at that point in time?

It was about 60,000. It was quite—that’s a good number of people. But everybody lived in houses so it looked a lot more dense than it really was cause most people they had some pretty big families. Like I said, the people across the street from me.
Were you involved, or were there any activities like boy scouts, or the parade lodges, or any other social activities or dances or things like that?

Well I joined the scouts, the boy scouts because when we moved from 129 (Elvin’s old house) to 74 (Elvin’s new house) there a man. He had been in WWI and he volunteered to be a scoutmaster and he knew a lot about – he was a woodsman. So he taught us a lot about discipline and things like that. We didn’t have any uniforms. We’d see the other scouts and we’d say, “where did they get those uniforms!? When are we going to get some!?” (Laughs)
Were any of your other brothers also in the scouts?
No I think they passed that up for other things. (Chuckles)
